rank.description: Position of the group in the tab, an integer from 1.

group.description: Places the plugin in its own group in the **Plugins** tab, separated from the rest. Omitted, the plugin joins the last group. Read as `item.group.name` / `item.group.rank`.

help.description: A help/support link for the plugin.

onlyofficeScheme.description: On desktop editors, serves the plugin through the `onlyoffice://` custom scheme instead of `file://`, so it gets a real origin with working CORS and a secure context.

offered.description: The plugin author who proposed the plugin for publication.

version.description: The plugin's own version, e.g. `"1.0"`. Optional per the reference, and genuinely omitted by shipped plugins - `guid`, `name` and `variations` are the only required top-level fields.

buttons.description: Defaults to no buttons (an empty toolbar) when omitted - routinely omitted in practice.

icons.description: Some plugins use the same rich per-scale shape here as `icons2` instead of a plain path/map.

isDisplayedInViewer.description: Hide a viewer-enabled variation from the viewer's plugin list after all. Only consulted when `isViewer` is `true`, and read as `isDisplayedInViewer !== false`.

isActivated.description:
Whether the created panel starts expanded (`true`, the default) or collapsed (`false`).

Panel variations only - `type` of `"panel"` or `"panelRight"`. The side-menu button and the panel are created either way; `false` only skips expanding it on render, leaving the user to open it from the button. Read as `isActivated !== false`, so omitting it and setting it to `true` are the same - only `false` does anything.

isViewer.description:
Offer this variation when the document is open read-only. Opt-in, default `false`: in edit mode a variation is listed regardless, and in viewer mode only `isViewer: true` puts it there - subject to `isDisplayedInViewer`, which can hide it again.

The editor's test is `isEdit || isViewer && isDisplayedInViewer !== false`. Note that  {@link  ButtonConfig.isViewer }  is the opposite: opt-out, shown unless set to `false`.

isVisual.description: Omitted in practice about as often as it's set explicitly.

lockReasons.description:
The reasons for blocking the editor toolbar that also disable the plugin button, for example `["reconnect", "disconnect"]` (see  {@link  ToolbarLockReason } ). Omitted or `null` (the default) disables the button whenever the toolbar is blocked.

While the document is loading or being refreshed, or the About panel is open, the button is always disabled, whatever the list says. Read from the first variation only.

methods.description: executeMethod names this variation calls - purely descriptive/documentation, not enforced.

screens.description: Store listing screenshots for this specific variation (see also StoreConfig.screenshots).

isViewer.description:
Hide this button when the document is open read-only. Opt-out: read as `isViewer !== false`, so the button shows in viewer mode unless this is `false`.

Note the opposite sense of  {@link  VariationConfig.isViewer } , which is opt-in and defaults to hidden. Same name, same file, inverted default.

style.description: Light/dark icon set variant - real-world config.json files pair this with `theme`.

theme.description: Icon theme name, e.g. `"flat"`/`"flatDark"` - not a fixed enum in practice.

default.description: Fallback used for any scale not otherwise listed.

ToolbarLockReason.description:
Why the editor blocks its toolbar - the values `VariationConfig.lockReasons` takes and the `onChangeButtonDisableState` event reports.

- `"not-loaded"` - the document is still loading.
- `"background-open"` - Cell only: the workbook is still being opened in the background.
- `"refresh-file"` - the file is being reloaded after an update.
- `"show-about"` - the About panel is open.
- `"reconnect"` - the connection to the server is lost and the editor is reconnecting.
- `"disconnect"` - editing is off until reopening: version history, license, editing error.
- `"unknown"` - Word, PDF and Visio: the co-editing session has been closed.
- `"mailmerge"` - Word only: a mail merge result is being previewed.
- `"signature"` - Word, Cell, Slide and PDF: the document carries digital signatures.
- `"send-for-signing"` - Word and PDF: the Send for signing panel is open.
- `"setlink"` - PDF only: the target of a link is being picked on a page.

The first four always disable plugin buttons, whatever `lockReasons` or `manageButtonState` say.

These are the reasons the current editor reports, not a closed set: a later editor version may add more, so any other string is accepted as well.

platforms.description: Where the plugin works: `web` - the editors in a browser, `desktop` - the desktop editors, in either of their modes (local files or a connected cloud). Omit it when the plugin works everywhere.

title: ONLYOFFICE Plugin config.json
description: Generated from PluginConfig (and the types it references) in index.d.ts - do not hand-edit, run `npm run generate-schema` instead.
